page: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a dedicated CPU server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture and AMD EPYC processors. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 188.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as a 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates under a QEMU hypervisor. No public IPv4 addresses are included by default, and there are no hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng scores placing the instance in the top 25% of tested hardware. Passmark CPU tests confirm this performance tier, showing strong results in extended instructions, encryption, and physics simulations. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is also in the top 25%, reaching 95.71 GB/sec, while read bandwidth and overall Passmark memory scores remain in the average range. The instance demonstrates strong performance in software compilation using Clang and ray tracing tasks. For database operations, Passmark database benchmarks place the server in the top 25%, complemented by average Redis SET throughput and static web serving capabilities. Large language model inference benchmarks show top-tier performance for text generation with small models, though performance scales down to average tiers for medium and large models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ccx63 delivers a high density of dedicated AMD EPYC resources and local NVMe storage without the overhead of bundled GPU hardware. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention, making it a viable option for CPU-heavy workloads. This resource profile is highly suited for multi-threaded software compilation, database hosting, ray tracing, and moderate-scale machine learning inference. It is also well-suited for general-purpose enterprise applications requiring predictable compute performance and fast local storage.
